title: How the ‘luteal uglies’ impact women during their periods
description:
Across social media young women are discussing the "luteal uglies." These are changes in appearance and mood that women experience during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle. We hear from women in Vietnam, the Philippines, and the UK about the symptoms they experience, from acne and bloating to fatigue and brain fog.

But what’s behind these changes? Dr Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains how changing hormone levels impact women’s bodies and their brains. She also offers some tips and coping strategies.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討近來在社群媒體上引發熱議的 luteal uglies 現象，指女性在月經來潮前約一週的黃體期內，因體內荷爾蒙劇烈波動而出現外貌與情緒上的負面變化。來自越南、菲律賓、加拿大與英國等地的女性分享了水腫、長痘痘、疲憊、腦霧、情緒敏感及社交意願降低等症狀。倫敦大學學院 UCL 生殖與分子遺傳學副教授 Helen O'Neill 博士解釋，排卵後雌激素與黃體素迅速下降，會促進皮脂分泌、導致水分滯留並減少血清素，進而引發皮膚問題、情緒低落與專注力下降。她建議女性透過記錄月經週期來掌握身體狀況，並保持適度運動、改善睡眠品質與避免飲酒來緩解不適，同時呼籲男性主動了解月經週期以給予女性更多理解與支持。
summaryEn: This episode of BBC's What in the World explores the social media trend known as the 'luteal uglies,' where women experience noticeable shifts in appearance and mood during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle, about a week before their period. Women from Vietnam, the Philippines, Canada, and the UK describe symptoms ranging from bloating, acne, and fatigue to brain fog, emotional sensitivity, and reduced motivation. Dr. Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains the underlying biology: rapid drops in estrogen and progesterone trigger increased sebum production, fluid retention, and lower serotonin levels, impacting skin, brain function, and mood. She advises women to track their cycles, maintain light exercise, improve sleep hygiene, and avoid alcohol, while encouraging men to educate themselves about menstrual health to better support the women in their lives.

And just one thing to add, which is that if you're listening to this and you've got concerns about your menstrual cycle, do speak to a doctor.
